title: What is the best AI financial advisor?
summary: The best AI financial advisors in 2026, compared on price, who stands behind the advice and whether they work with the accounts you already have.
body_markdown:
## Which AI financial advisors are worth using?


### PortfolioPilot: best for a detailed second opinion


PortfolioPilot comes from Global Predictions, an SEC-registered investment adviser. It connects to more than 12,000 brokerages, banks and crypto wallets, scores your portfolio and suggests changes that you review and decide on. Its assistant answers questions in plain language.


The free plan tracks your net worth. Gold costs $29 a month or $240 a year and adds recommendations and limited use of the assistant. Platinum costs $99 a month or $588 a year with unlimited use, and Pro costs $149 a month or $1,188 a year and adds a quarterly call with a product expert. PortfolioPilot can’t place trades and has no native app, though its site is built to work on phones.


### Range: best for AI plus a human team


Range Advisory is an SEC-registered investment adviser that pairs its AI, Rai, with a team of advisers that includes CFPs and CFA charterholders. Members message Rai and their team about investments, taxes, equity compensation and estate questions, and Range manages the portfolio with no asset-based fee and no asset minimum.


Premium costs $3,950 a year. Platinum, at $6,950, adds CPAs, tax projections, personal tax filing and estate documents, and Titanium, at $12,500, covers more complex returns. Fund, custodian and other third-party fees can apply on top.


### Magnifi: best for finding new investment ideas


Magnifi LLC is an SEC-registered investment adviser. Its AI answers plain-English questions about your holdings and analyzes risk and diversification. It also helps you screen stocks and funds and test how a new investment would fit before you buy it. It connects brokerage, IRA, 401(k) and HSA accounts.


The free plan covers portfolio analysis, discovery and commission-free trading from the app. Premium costs $14 a month or $99 a year and adds scenario analysis, forecasting and weekly summaries.


### Origin: best for budgeting with an adviser behind it


Origin is a money app whose AI Financial Advisor follows your spending and investing, offered through Origin Investment Advisory, an SEC-registered investment adviser. It builds and tracks a budget, finds subscriptions, lets a partner join at no extra cost and connects accounts through Plaid, MX and Mastercard.


Origin also runs an automated index portfolio with no asset-based fee, starting from $1, though custodian fees can apply. Its app offers one-on-one meetings with CFP professionals, along with tax filing and estate planning.


### Betterment: best for a managed index portfolio


Betterment is a robo-advisor, offered by Betterment LLC, an SEC-registered investment adviser. You move money into a Betterment account, and it builds and manages a portfolio for you. The digital plan costs $5 a month, or 0.25% a year once you have $24,000 invested or set up $200 a month in recurring deposits.


Premium costs 0.65% a year on the first $1 million, needs $100,000 in eligible investments and adds unlimited access to CFP professionals. You can link outside accounts to see them in Betterment, but its advice doesn’t take the specific investments you hold elsewhere into account.


### Our top pick: Astor


Astor is a personal investing agent on iPhone and in iMessage, offered by Gaus, Inc., an SEC-registered investment adviser, so its recommendations are personalized investment advice and it owes clients a fiduciary duty. It connects through Plaid to the brokerage, retirement and crypto accounts you already have at most major US institutions, like Robinhood, Schwab and Coinbase. It can see your holdings but can’t move money, and you don’t transfer anything to it.


Astor follows every position you own, along with the earnings dates, filings and headlines that touch them and the themes you follow. When something crosses a line you care about, it texts you what happened, why it matters to you and what you could do, and it stays quiet when nothing matters.[At a glance](https://www.astor.app/blog/at-a-glance) gives you a five-second read on your day, and[scheduled alerts](https://www.astor.app/blog/scheduled-alerts) let you ask for a check every morning or before a company you own reports.


You can[text Astor in iMessage](https://www.astor.app/blog/talk-to-astor-in-imessage) to ask about your actual holdings, and its answers use live prices, news and filings, with the reasoning and sources behind every alert. On Max plans,[Text to Trade](https://www.astor.app/blog/introducing-text-to-trade) turns an idea into a basket of companies sized against what you own and the budget you set, and you approve every trade before it executes in your own Robinhood agentic account.


Astor is free to start with no card, and the free plan includes one custom alert. Pro and Max are in the table above and on the[pricing page](https://www.astor.app/pricing) , and they’re a flat price, never a percentage of your assets.
